text:
sre-oncall: starting canary rollout of nvidia-driver 550.102 to us-west2 gpu pool, will target 3 nodes first. monitoring dkms builds and boot loops :rotating_light:

matt: seeing 2/3 canary nodes reprovisioned but they never finish booting, stuck in initramfs with modprobe timeouts

matt: paste of dmesg on node ip-10-0-2-14:
```
[   12.345678] modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-101-generic
[   12.345689] nvidia-uvm: probe of nvidia-uvm failed with error -2
[   12.345700] init: could not start secure boot checks, continuing
[   60.123456] systemd[1]: Timed out waiting for device dev-disk-by
```

anya: DKMS logs show compile error referencing mismatched kernel headers. looks like host image still at linux-headers 5.15.0-99 while kernel is 5.15.0-101. probably image sync issue from our prebake job.

ritesh: also saw rmmod failures leaving devices busy, which blocks the new module install. example from /var/log/syslog:
```
Aug 23 02:14:01 ip-10-0-2-14 kernel: rmmod: ERROR: remove 'nvidia-uvm' failed: Device or resource busy
Aug 23 02:14:01 ip-10-0-2-14 kernel: rmmod: module nvidia_uvm is in use
```

ritesh: tl;dr likely race between container runtimes (pods still attached) and our reprovision path trying to rmmod/install. dkms install then fails because leftover module dir causes version mismatch.

sre-oncall: ok pausing rollout. canary nodes quarantined and traffic shifted. tagging incident for infra-runbook:driver-upgrades.

matt: doing quick check: dkms status on one failed node:
```
dkms status
nvidia, 510.60.02, 5.15.0-101-generic, x86_64: installed
nvidia, 550.102, 5.15.0-101-generic, x86_64: added
```
matt: shows added but not installed, so post-install hooks probably aborted.

anya: workaround idea: before reprovision we should drain pods with force=false and wait up to 2m for kube to detach GPU devices, then rmmod. also ensure linux-headers package matches kernel commit.

ritesh: another symptom: NCCL init fails in some tests after partial driver install, logs show "NCCL WARN Call to cuInit failed" and processes leak file handles to /dev/nvidiactl which prevents module removal.

matt: can reproduce locally with two steps: start a test pod with CUDA container, kill kubelet right as it releases GPU -> device stays open, rmmod fails. quick fix: `lsof /dev/nvidia*` to find PIDs and kill, then rmmod. but not safe at scale.

deploy-bot: provisioner: [us-west2-gpu-canary] node ip-10-0-2-14 reprovision FAILED at 1998765436 - rolling back to previous driver 535.45. 3 nodes affected.

sre-oncall: action items:
- (ritesh) add pre-reprovision step to check for open fds on /dev/nvidia* and surface in CI (short term).
- (anya) fix prebake job to ensure linux-headers sync and add a post-bake header check (medium term).
- (matt) add a staging reprovision that drains pods gracefully and runs a verify script that checks dkms status and modprobe nvidia (short term).

anya: will open a PR for header sync and a runbook section for forced-detach cases.

matt: adding a small smoke test to our canary run that launches a CUDA container, runs simple nvcc test and then deletes pod to catch detach races.

ritesh: we should also consider making dkms install idempotent by cleaning old module dirs before install if safe. leaving note for research.

sre-oncall: thanks all. keeping this thread open for updates. if anyone sees new failed nodes, ping here and escalate to oncall for rollback. :thumbsup:
